cue: How do you say someone is really good at what they do?

es.meaning: To be extremely good at a particular activity.
es.example: Pídele a ella que revise los números: es un hacha con las hojas de cálculo.
es.exampleTranslation: Ask her to check the figures — she's brilliant with spreadsheets.
es.regionNote: Attested in Spain and Mexico; may read as traditional next to newer slang. Reviewer to confirm currency.

it.meaning: To be capable, sharp and dependable — as a person, not only at one task.
it.example: Il ragazzo nuovo è in gamba: in due settimane ha imparato tutto il reparto.
it.exampleTranslation: The new lad is sharp — he learned the whole department in a fortnight.

bridge.note: Spanish sharpens you into a tool; Italian stands you upright. Un hacha is an axe — praise aimed at a skill, and it wants a domain to point at: an axe at maths, an axe at spreadsheets. In gamba is a whole person on their own two legs, capable and sound, and needs no object at all. The Italian also does something the Spanish never does: it says goodbye. Sta' in gamba is a farewell, take care of yourself — and no Spanish speaker would guess that an axe could do the same job.

interference.es_to_it: Do not look for the tool. 'Essere un'ascia' means nothing in Italian. And note the widening: in gamba praises the person, not the skill, so it does not want 'in gamba con i numeri' the way Spanish wants 'un hacha con los números' — for a specific talent Italian says 'è bravo con i numeri' or 'è un mago dei numeri'.
interference.it_to_es: Spanish narrows. Ser un hacha nearly always names the field it applies to, and it never works as a farewell — the Italian 'sta' in gamba' at the end of a message has no Spanish equivalent in this family; Spanish would use 'cuídate'.

review.notes: Drafted by Claude 2026-08-01, batch 2 (CANDIDATES.md Top picks 18). SOURCES NOT HUMAN-VERIFIED — standard headword URLs, not opened. RAE should carry 'ser un hacha' under `hacha`; Treccani should carry 'in gamba' under `gamba`. SCOPE MISMATCH IS DELIBERATE AND IS THE ENTRY'S POINT, but it is also the entry's weakness: ser un hacha is domain-bound, essere in gamba is person-general, so they are not clean equivalents. If the reviewers judge the gap too wide to call a pairing, the alternates logged in CANDIDATES.md are 'ser un crack' and 'estar espabilado' for the general-competence sense.
